title: FloatAP: Supporting High-Performance Floating-Point Arithmetic in Associative Processors
problem: Associative Processors lack efficient floating-point arithmetic support due to insufficient computational throughput when using traditional bit-serial approaches. This limits their applicability to critical AI/ML and scientific workloads that require FP computation.
motivation: Floating-point support is crucial for many critical AI/ML and scientific workloads, and enabling efficient FP arithmetic in APs could unlock their high data-parallelism benefits for these domains.
method: FloatAP speeds up floating-point math on associative processors by aligning multiple floating-point numbers in parallel—simultaneously adjusting the decimal points of several numbers so they can be added correctly. Rather than computing multiplication bit-by-bit like traditional systems, it reuses the processor's existing hardware for adding (called adder trees) to handle multiplication and dot product operations. The approach supports standard vector programming through the RISC-V 'V' extension and works with different floating-point formats and integer operations.
key_novelty: This is the first programmable associative processor that enables efficient floating-point arithmetic through parallel alignment of multiple floating-point numbers (handling multiple bits and components simultaneously) and by repurposing the processor's existing addition hardware for multiplication.
contributions: First highly programmable AP architecture tailored for high-performance floating-point arithmetic
Bit- and component-parallel vector mantissa alignment method for efficient FP addition and reduction
Adder tree repurposing for efficient FP multiplication and dot product operations
RISC-V 'V' vector extension support with ML framework compatibility and multi-format FP support

metrics.speedup: 2.7× vs NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU for single-precision FP (1.5× for bfloat16)
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.4× higher energy efficiency vs A100 (1.6× for bfloat16)

limitations: Limitations and future work not discussed in abstract.
